entities.summary: Brigid of Kildare (b. 453 CE, Faughart) was a religious figure and entrepreneur of the Classical era, active in Faughart and Kildare. She played a crucial role in the establishment of the monastery of Kildare, which became a major center of learning and spirituality in medieval Ireland. Brigid's leadership and spiritual guidance helped to spread Christianity throughout Ireland, and her legacy continued to inspire generations of Irish monks and nuns. The monastery of Kildare also became a center of art and culture, producing works of illuminated manuscripts and metalwork that showcased the skills of Irish artisans. Brigid's impact on Irish history extends beyond her own lifetime, as her legacy influenced the development of Irish identity and culture. The monastery of Kildare was also a major pilgrimage site, attracting visitors from across Europe. In 543 CE, Brigid founded the monastery of Clonmacnoise, which became a major center of learning and spirituality in medieval Ireland. Her death in 525 CE marked the end of an era, but her legacy continued to inspire generations of Irish leaders and spiritual figures. The site of Kildare was reburied in 1168 CE, and the remains were placed in a church built by King Henry II of England. The monastery of Kildare was destroyed by Viking invaders in the 9th century, but the site was rebuilt and reestablished as a major center of learning and spirituality in medieval Ireland.
